themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 13 this week—a 940% jump from the 1.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting either a sudden crackdown, new vendor activity, or emerging permit/licensing violations in Borough Park/Kensington.
evidence: 13 vendor enforcement complaints this week vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (940% spike, z-score 9.05)
Signal is statistically significant (z-score 9.05, severity rated high)
No prior news mentions or Reddit discussion suggests this is under-reported locally
reporting_angles: Has NYPD or Department of Consumer Affairs launched a new enforcement action against street vendors in the district?
Are vendors reporting harassment or permit denials; is this a supply-side crackdown or demand-side complaint surge?

themes_detail.label: Bike/Skate Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about bikes, roller skates, or skateboards jumped to 3 this week—a 2,300% increase from the 0.1 weekly baseline—indicating either new youth activity, safety concerns, or enforcement focus on micro-mobility in the neighborhood.
evidence: 3 bike/roller/skate complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Statistically extreme deviation (z-score 8.69) despite low absolute volume
No contextual news or Reddit discussion to explain the spike
reporting_angles: Is there a new skate park, bike lane, or youth gathering spot attracting activity?
Are residents complaining about safety hazards, or is this enforcement against unpermitted activity?

themes_detail.label: Missed Garbage Collection Surge
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints nearly quadrupled to 29 this week—a 364% spike from the 6.2 weekly average—indicating possible sanitation service breakdowns, staffing issues, or route failures in the district.
evidence: 29 missed collection complaints this week vs. 6.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (364% spike, z-score 4.6)
This is the most concrete absolute-volume spike among recent signals
Converges with long-standing CB budget pressure for enhanced sanitation infrastructure
reporting_angles: Has Sanitation Department had truck breakdowns, staffing cuts, or route changes this week?
Which streets/blocks are most affected; is this a single-route failure or district-wide issue?

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Complaints (2 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 14 two weeks ago—a 211% jump from the 4.5 weekly baseline—suggesting possible pest, disease, or environmental health concerns that may still be unresolved.
evidence: 14 dead animal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (211% spike, z-score 4.36)
Signal is 2 weeks old, so may have already been addressed or may indicate ongoing infestation
Suggests potential sanitation or rodent control issue worth follow-up
reporting_angles: Was there a specific die-off event (contaminated food, disease outbreak) or ongoing rodent/pest problem?
Has NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene responded; are residents still reporting dead animals?

themes_detail.label: Building Electrical & Inspection Surge (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints and Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints both spiked 3 weeks ago (4 and 5 complaints respectively, up 540% and 567% from baseline)—suggesting possible structural or code violations discovered in a cluster of buildings.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score 4.85)
5 SPIT complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% spike, z-score 6.43)
Convergence of electrical + inspection signals suggests possible building-code enforcement action or discovered violations
Aligns with CB's repeated requests for additional DOB building inspectors
reporting_angles: Did Department of Buildings initiate an enforcement sweep 3 weeks ago; which buildings were flagged?
Are electrical code violations tied to aging housing stock or new construction issues?
